sentences.text: 1). The present appeal u/s 29 of Protection of Women from Domestic Case.

No. 162/2023 Sachin v.
Jyoti page 1 of 5 Violence Act 2005 is filed by the husband Sachin Yadav (hereinafter referred to as appellant) thereby challenging the impugned order dated 18.05.2023 passed by Ld. MM, Mahila Court-01, PHC, New Delhi vide which interim maintenance @ Rs.40,000/- per month was granted to Respondent/wife.
TCR of the case was also summoned.

2). Vide the present appeal, appellant has contended that the Ld. MM has wrongly appreciated the bank statements placed on record as well as wrongly assessed the income of the Appellant to the tune of Rs. 1.5 Lakhs.
He further contended that the Ld. MM has wrongly appreciated that the appellant belongs to landlord family and is receiving income from various properties, in the absence of any documentary evidence.
He further alleged that the parties are living separately from last 15 years.
He further contended that the said order is passed without application of mind.
Further, he submitted that it is not possible for the appellant to pay Rs.40,000/- pm interim maintenance.

1 3).
Ld counsel for the respondent wish not to file the written reply and orally argued the appeal.

Ld.
Counsel for the respondent argued that Ld. MM has rightly appreciated the property documents placed on record as well as the bank statements of the appellant.
4). I have considered the arguments addressed by the appellant as well as the respondent and have also perused the trial court record.
5). The object of interim maintenance is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of failure of marriage.

The said amount has to be determined on the basis of the status of the parties, reasonable needs of wife, independent source of income of Case. No. 162/2023 Sachin v. Jyoti page 2 of 5 the applicant etc.

For determining these factors,
court has to look into the income affidavits filed by both the parties and the documents filed alongwith the said affidavit.
There is no straight jacket formula for fixing the quantum of interim maintenance.
A careful and just balance must be drawn between all relevant factors.

6). To prima-facie show the income of husband, it is for the wife to show the documents as to the income of the husband, however practically in most of the cases such evidence would never be readily available to the wife.

Therefore, generally it would be for the husband to prove his real income on record otherwise adverse inference or presumption as to income needs to be drawn while determining the amount of maintenance.
Unfortunately, as usual, here in this case also the appellant/husband has failed to brought on record relevant documents so as to show a clear picture about his real earnings.

Infact appellant had made contradictory statements as to his income i.e. on one occasion he stated that he is earning Rs.8000/- per month whereas in his income affidavit, he stated that he is earning Rs.22,500/- per month.
This court is conscious of the fact that appellant was not working anywhere and is earning his livelihood from various other sources, which the appellant has not truly disclosed.

It cannot be ignored that though the court has to rely upon the documents placed on record, however, court can infer the earning capacity of the person when he came forward with a story that he does not have sufficient income.
7). Therefore, in order to decide the present appeal, it would be necessary to refer to the bank statements as well as the other documents filed by the appellant.

Various statements of bank account of the appellant Case. No. 162/2023 Sachin v. Jyoti page 3 of 5 have been filed alongwith the present appeal thereby showing that appellant is maintaining multiple bank accounts.
It is not necessary to refer to the each and every entry of every bank account detail which are on record.

Suffice it to note that in every bank statement there are various cash deposits from time to time which manifests that the appellant has not disclosed his true income and also the fact that the appellant has various other sources of income.
Perusal of the bank statement, shows that there are multiple transactions which are running into lacs of rupees.
Thus, the argument that the appellant was earning only Rs. 8000/- or Rs.22,000/- pm is running against the entries shown in the different bank statements of the appellant.
Hence, the Ld. MM has rightly drawn the presumption as to income of appellant to be somewhere between 1-1.5 Lakhs.
Furthermore admittedly, in the present case, the appellant alongwith his brother had received approx. Rs.9 crore as a compensation amount in land acquisition proceedings.

Further, appellant is Sachin Yadav vs State on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197016672/
2 also receiving amount of Rs.1.5 lacs per annum as royalty in lieu of acquisition of said land.

Also Ld.
MM has rightly considered that the Appellant has proprietor interest in various ancestral properties,
which fact is relevant to point towards the status of the Appellant.

8). On the other hand, the documents filed by the respondent indicate that she has no independent source of income except the interest income from the FD of Rs.8 lacs and the same would not generate even a fraction of the amount needed to maintain her with the life style even remotely similar to what appellant may be enjoying.
Case. No. 162/2023 Sachin v. Jyoti page 4 of 5
9). Therefore, in these circumstances, the present appeal is dismissed and the order dated 18.05.2023 passed by Ld. MM Mahila Court-01, PHC, New Delhi is upheld.
10). Copy of the instant order alongwith trial court record be sent to the Ld. Trial Court concerned.
11). File of criminal appeal be consigned to record room.
Announced in Open Court On 16th August, 2023.
(Sanjay Khanagwal)
